clusters.name: Secondary school and family separation, 1987
clusters.reason: Around the time you started secondary school, your stepparents separated over having a baby, you made the chess squad and felt out of your depth, and your relationship with your stepfather stayed distant while you sought your father's attention. These shifts in family closeness and your own anxiety piled up together.

clusters.name: Leaving home and first major loss, 1989–1994
clusters.reason: Your grandfather died in mid-1991 just as you'd left for conservatory, you hurt your wrist and couldn't play, fell into heavy use and isolation, your grandmother had thyroid surgery, and your mother married Desmond. Within these shifts your functioning dropped, anxiety rose, and you cycled through fusion with your roommate Rafe, then conflict and distance. An exchange to Portugal in early 1994 lifted you out of it. The loss of your grandfather and the collision of leaving home seem to have opened a long stretch of trouble.
clusters.change: You moved away to conservatory the autumn after your grandfather's stroke in June 1991; the timing suggests his death that summer sat among the events that made leaving harder.

clusters.name: High-performing years and early split, 1998–1999
clusters.reason: You were playing the best you ever had and winning competitions, but insomnia began interfering with performances. You and Joelle split up around mid-1999, and you started therapy with Victor after the break. The gap between your functioning rising and your symptoms rising, all within your relationship, suggests the split turned what had been manageable into something you needed help with.

clusters.name: Burnout, loss of grandmother and depression, 2001–2004
clusters.reason: You ran out of steam for performing in 2001 while your grandmother was found to have bowel cancer and underwent surgery and chemotherapy. You failed a disastrous audition in early 2002 and left Thornbury for Gull Harbour, distancing from family and friends. You met Marisol in winter 2003 and moved to Fenwick with her, then split that autumn and sank into deep depression. You couldn't face your parents, relied on friends like Corbin and Hamish instead, and your grandmother died in early 2004. You began swimming and returned to therapy, and your functioning began to lift. This is the stretch you named as ages 27 to 29.

clusters.name: Nursing school and cutoff from mother, 2008–2010
clusters.reason: Your grandmother Lorna died in January 2008 and your grandfather Clifford died around the same time. You took four weeks at Alder Creek building with Silas that summer, too drained for contact with your mother. She pressed you to visit despite your saying the timing was wrong, you kept the door shut on her when she came anyway, and then you stopped speaking to her when you moved to Marlow Sound for nursing school in August. The silence held roughly a year. Your aunt Imogen had a stroke and months of rehab within this stretch. The loss of both grandparents, your own depleted state, and the conflict with your mother when she pushed past your boundary seem to have opened the cutoff.

clusters.name: Marriage and family proximity, 2017–2019
clusters.reason: You married Wren in March 2017 and saw your mother less often once her family came into your life. Your cousin Alice was diagnosed with MS in late 2017. Your sister Tara married James and had a baby on the way by late 2019. Your partner's family is fused and talks all day; in late October 2019 when her mother retired and the family gathered at the lake, Wren was swamped with events, you overfunctioned to settle her, and you lost sleep from the small hours onward, anxious and distant from the family around you. At the same time your job steadied and paid well, easing strain, but you remain constantly anxious that you should be driving projects forward. Small regular contact with your mother has helped soften old distance. The strain of living close to her fused family and your own keyed-up state sit together in this period.
clusters.change: Your marriage brought you into regular contact with Wren's tightly connected family; the lake weekend in late October 2019 shows the strain of that proximity alongside your own anxiety and sleep trouble around family occasions.

periods.name: the year I left home
periods.words: The first is the year I left home: I went off to the conservatory, hurt my wrist in the first term and couldn't play, dropped out and drifted at my mother's place, then spent a bleak spell at the community college shooting pool every night until an exchange in Portugal snapped me out of it and I tore through the rest of my coursework.

periods.name: the long slump
periods.words: The second is the long slump, roughly ages 27 to 29, when nothing at home felt right, I moved to Gull Harbour away from nearly everyone I knew, then followed Marisol to Fenwick, and when that fell apart I went under, a depression I only really climbed out of after nursing school.
